title: Managing and scoping React Native upgrades
summary: Learn tips and tricks for handling React Native upgrades from the perspective of Rippling’s Engineering team.
body_text: At Rippling, our journey with React Native has been a key part of building mobile applications that are fast, reliable, and feature-rich. With more than five years of experience using React Native, we've harnessed its ability to share code across platforms and enable collaboration between web and mobile engineers, allowing us to deliver seamless product integrations efficiently. The React Native community moves quickly, with frequent updates and releases. Staying up-to-date with these rapid changes is essential for maintaining the security, performance, and compatibility of our apps— Rippling Mobile and Rippling Kiosk . Initially, we upgraded every year, but we've since transitioned to semi-annual major upgrades, reflecting a more structured approach to managing the fast-paced evolution of React Native. While these upgrades can be challenging, they offer substantial benefits, such as access to new APIs, improved developer tools, and optimized performance. In this blog, we’ll take you behind the scenes at Rippling, sharing our strategies for scoping and managing React Native upgrades. From allocating dedicated resources to overcoming specific challenges, we’ll provide insights into how we balance the disruption of an upgrade with its long-term advantages, making sure our apps continue to deliver exceptional experiences for employees. Rippling’s mobile apps: A brief overview Rippling has two mobile applications, each serving distinct purposes for different user groups: App name Audience & Purpose Features Store Availability Rippling Mobile App Employees - Offers a unified platform for employees to manage various HR, Finance, and IT-related tasks. - Time and Attendance : Track work hours and attendance patterns - Payroll : View salary details and manage pay-related information - Spend Management : Expense reimbursements - Time Off : Apply for and manage leaves - Benefits : Explore and manage employee benefits Google: Play Store Apple: App Store Rippling Kiosk App Hourly employees of companies - A dedicated app for clocking in and out of shifts, ensuring streamlined time tracking for hourly workers. - Clock in/out Pin Based - Manage shifts Google: Play Store Apple: App Store Both apps undergo 200+ releases annually and integrate with more than 10 products , showcasing the scale and complexity of the systems we manage. With a mix of 53% focused on bug fixes, performance, and stability improvements, and 47% introducing new features, these frequent releases are key to maintaining app reliability and driving innovation. Over the years, Rippling has consistently embraced updates in React Native to stay aligned with the evolving ecosystem. These frequent updates and integrations highlight the dynamic nature of our mobile platform and our commitment to continuously improving the user experience, ensuring both apps remain performant, reliable, and up to date with modern development standards. Why Rippling upgrades React Native These upgrades are essential for ensuring our apps remain secure, high-performing, and aligned with the latest technology standards. Here are the key reasons why we prioritize regular upgrades, along with a look at how they’ve directly benefited our engineering efforts: 1. Access to new features: Upgrading unlocks new features and performance optimizations that directly enhance our apps. For example, during our upgrade to React Native 0.70, we saw significant improvements with the introduction of Hermes as the default JavaScript engine . This change reduced our JavaScript bundle load time by more than 50%, improving app launch speeds and delivering a noticeably smoother user experience. 2. Security improvements: With each upgrade, we ensure that our apps are protected against vulnerabilities through critical security patches. This proactive approach helps safeguard sensitive user data and meets compliance standards expected by businesses using Rippling. 3. Bug fixes and stability enhancements: New versions address existing bugs and stability issues, minimizing downtime and making troubleshooting easier. For example, during the upgrade from 0.72 to 0.73, we benefited from fixes to previously reported crashes in edge-case scenarios, leading to a more stable application. 4. Compatibility with third-party libraries: Upgrades help us maintain compatibility with the third-party libraries we rely on. As we upgraded to React Native 0.72, the improved support for TypeScript allowed us to better integrate type safety into our codebase, reducing runtime errors and making our development process more robust. 5. Support for new React, iOS, and Android versions: Each major upgrade aligns our apps with updated React versions, the latest Android and iOS operating systems, and essential development tools like Android Studio and Xcode. For example, upgrading to React Native 0.72 ensured our apps were optimized for the latest macOS and Xcode upgrades, making it easier for engineers to maintain and enhance the product. 6. Fulfilling policy requirements: The mobile app ecosystem is constantly evolving, with Apple and Google frequently updating their policies. Regular upgrades help us meet these requirements seamlessly. For instance, our recent upgrades ensured that our apps complied with the latest iOS App Store and Google Play Store submission guidelines. Failure to keep up with these updates could lead to serious consequences, including app rejection, removal from the stores, revenue loss, and damage to user trust. By staying compliant, we not only avoid these risks but also ensure the continued availability of our app, maintaining both our user base and brand reputation. 7. Future-proofing through end-of-life awareness: Staying informed about React Native’s End-of-Life (EOL) policies is vital. Running an unsupported version risks exposing apps to security vulnerabilities and integration issues with third-party libraries. Regular upgrades, such as our recent transition from 0.70 to 0.73, ensure that our apps remain compliant, secure, and easy to maintain, while also benefiting from community support and updated resources. Understanding the upgrade process Upgrading React Native isn’t just about updating a library—it’s a comprehensive process that touches multiple layers of your application. At Rippling, we recently upgraded from React Native 0.72 to 0.73 , which provides a practical example of the considerations and adjustments involved. 1. JavaScript code: One of the first steps in the upgrade was reviewing our JavaScript codebase. The new version introduced changes to APIs, requiring us to replace deprecated methods and adjust functionality. For instance, we refactored parts of our code to align with stricter type-checking enforced by the updated TypeScript version, ensuring smoother runtime behavior and reducing errors. 2. Native code: This upgrade required updates to our native Android and iOS codebases. With the new version of React Native, support for the latest iOS and Android operating systems was introduced. We adjusted files like build.gradle for Android and Podfile for iOS to ensure compatibility, enabling our apps to leverage platform-specific enhancements and policies. 3. Third-Party dependencies: Several third-party libraries we rely on, such as React Navigation and Detox needed updates to stay compatible with React Native 0.73. During the process, we resolved conflicts arising from outdated dependencies and ensured that their latest versions worked seamlessly within our app ecosystem. 4. Configuration files: Key configuration files like AndroidManifest.xml and Info.plist required minor changes to meet the latest requirements. For instance, we updated permissions and configurations to comply with the latest Android and iOS store submission guidelines, ensuring our apps met policy standards. 5. CI/CD pipelines: Our CI/CD pipelines also underwent modifications. The upgrade introduced updated build requirements, prompting us to adjust our workflows in Bitrise and GitHub Actions. This ensured that builds were efficient and aligned with the new version’s dependencies and testing frameworks. 6. Static analysis tools: As part of our commitment to maintaining high code quality, we upgraded static analysis tools like TypeScript , ESLint , and Prettier . These upgrades enabled us to use new rules and improved error detection, particularly beneficial for catching issues during the early stages of development. 7. Other development tools: We also updated our debugging tools and IDEs, such as Android Studio and Xcode , to their latest versions. These updates offered better support for React Native 0.73, improved performance during development, and provided access to new debugging features that simplified troubleshooting. Key lessons learned from the past upgrades: Plan for dependencies: Upgrading third-party libraries alongside React Native is critical to avoid compatibility issues. Test incrementally: Running tests throughout the process helped us catch bugs early and minimized disruption to ongoing development. Optimize CI/CD: Updating CI/CD pipelines early in the process ensured seamless integration and deployment once the upgrade was complete. Communicate clearly: Having one engineer dedicated to the upgrade allowed us to minimize disruption to feature development while maintaining clear communication with the broader team. By following a structured approach, we ensured that the transition was smooth, enabling Rippling Mobile and Rippling Kiosk to take full advantage of React Native 0.73’s new features and improvements. This upgrade was not just a technical necessity—it was an investment in the future scalability and performance of our apps. Adopting a gradual approach At Rippling, we've found that adopting a gradual approach is one of the most effective strategies for managing React Native upgrades. Instead of tackling the entire application at once, we break the process into smaller, manageable steps. This incremental method allows us to: Mitigate risks: Address potential issues in a controlled manner by upgrading specific features or components step by step Maintain functionality: Ensure that the application remains operational throughout the upgrade process, minimizing disruption to end users Facilitate testing and validation: Focus on smaller, isolated changes that are easier to test and validate, ensuring stability and compatibility Integrate enhancements seamlessly: Gradual upgrades make it easier to incorporate and leverage new React Native features and improvements without overwhelming the development process This approach has proven invaluable in managing complexity and delivering a more resilient application. By prioritizing stability and user experience, a phased strategy helps us maximize the benefits of upgrading while minimizing disruptions. Scoping the Upgrade Before beginning the React Native upgrade process, it’s critical to scope the changes comprehensively. This step ensures that the transition is well-planned and minimizes disruptions to your application. Here’s how we approach scoping at Rippling: 1. Reviewing the changelog Action: Analyze the official React Native changelog for all versions included in the upgrade path. Purpose: Gain a clear understanding of changes, deprecated APIs, and new features that might impact your app. Benefit: This helps anticipate the necessary modifications and plan the upgrade steps effectively. 2. Consulting the React Native blog Action : Explore the React Native blog to stay updated with announcements, insights, and detailed upgrade guides from the core team. Purpose : Gain a deeper understanding of major updates, migration strategies, and the latest features to better align your upgrade process with React Native's best practices. Benefit : Leverage expert guidance to streamline the upgrade, minimize risks, and effectively utilize new enhancements in your application. 3. Using upgrade helper tools Tools: We leverage the React Native Upgrade Helper and Expo Native Project Upgrade Helper to streamline our upgrade process. Functionality: These tools highlight the differences between the current and target versions, simplifying the identification of required changes. Using the Upgrade Helper, we can quickly pinpoint necessary code adjustments and configurations for JavaScript and Native code. Expo CNG (Continuous Native Generation) adoption : To further simplify and accelerate our upgrade process, we’re planning to adopt Expo CNG (Continuous Native Generation) soon. Expo CNG introduces an innovative approach by providing a continuous integration system that handles the generation of native code. This helps eliminate manual processes traditionally involved with managing native code changes, reducing friction and increasing the speed of upgrades. By leveraging Expo CNG, we expect even smoother native updates, quicker iterations, and better alignment with modern development practices. Adopting Expo CNG is a strategic step forward, not only improving our internal development workflows but also contributing to the Expo ecosystem. By relying on Expo’s powerful infrastructure, we can more easily manage native dependencies, reduce the risk of incompatibilities, and keep both of our mobile apps performing optimally with minimal overhead. 4. Updating dependencies Process: Audit all third-party libraries and confirm compatibility with the target React Native version. Tools: Use npm outdated or yarn outdated to identify outdated packages. Action: Check each dependency’s repository for migration guides and updates. 5. Evaluating custom code Scope: Review any custom code or patches applied to the React Native framework. Outcome: Ensure customizations align with the updated framework and plan necessary adjustments. 6. Reviewing security implications Focus: Examine security updates or requirements in the target version. Action: Verify compliance with new security practices to safeguard user data. 7. Mapping features and impact Approach: Create a detailed list of app features and identify those impacted by the upgrade. Outcome: This enables prioritization and planning for potential adjustments or testing needs. 8. Prioritizing upgrades Strategy: Tackle critical features and high-impact areas first, leaving less essential components for later phases. Result: This ensures that vital functionality remains intact throughout the upgrade process. 9. Assessing performance metrics Baseline: Gather pre-upgrade performance data to compare with post-upgrade metrics. Objective: Identify and address any regressions introduced during the update. 10. Establishing rollback procedures Plan: Document a rollback strategy to revert to the previous version if significant issues arise. Impact: This reduces downtime and ensures a quick recovery if unexpected problems occur. 11. Team communication Engagement: Involve the team in planning discussions to gather input on potential challenges. Alignment: Make sure everyone understands the upgrade strategy and their responsibilities. By following this structured approach to scoping, we ensure a smoother upgrade process that minimizes risks, reduces surprises, and prepares the team to tackle challenges effectively. This proactive planning lays the foundation for a successful React Native upgrade while maintaining stability and performance. Compatibility with third-party libraries: A major risk One of the most significant risks we encountered was third-party library compatibility. Many of our dependencies were not immediately compatible with the latest React Native version, which introduced delays and additional troubleshooting steps. To manage this risk: Early compatibility assessment: We reviewed each dependency and checked for compatibility information or recent updates on their repositories. Temporary forks and custom patches: For critical libraries lacking official updates, we created temporary forks and modified the code ourselves. This helped us keep the upgrade on track while waiting for library maintainers to release official patches. Exploring alternatives: When certain libraries seemed unlikely to receive updates soon, we researched alternative solutions that were compatible with the new React Native version. Dependency compatibility is a crucial risk factor during upgrades. Approaching it with a proactive strategy minimized disruptions, allowing us to maintain the app’s functionality throughout the process. Effort and team Involvement in RN upgrades At Rippling, the RN upgrade process typically requires six to eight engineer weeks , depending on the scope and complexity of the upgrade. The effort is primarily led by a single dedicated engineer who drives the upgrade process while collaborating with other team members as needed. This ensures minimal disruption to ongoing feature development, as most of the team continues to focus on their regular work. Cross-functional input is occasionally required to address issues in specific product modules and to verify that the upgrade does not introduce regressions. Automating the upgrade process At Rippling, we prioritize efficiency in our upgrade workflows by automating key steps of the React Native upgrade process. Leveraging tools and scripts helps us streamline the process, reduce manual effort, and minimize errors. Some of the tools we use or recommend include: React Native Upgrade Helper : A community-driven tool that provides a detailed, side-by-side comparison of changes required for upgrading to a specific version of React Native. This helps ensure we don’t miss critical updates in configuration files or dependencies. Expo Native Project Upgrade Helper : For projects using Expo, this tool offers a similar experience by highlighting the necessary adjustments to seamlessly transition to newer versions. Custom scripts: We have developed in-house scripts to automate repetitive tasks, such as dependency checks and static analysis tool upgrades, ensuring a consistent approach to upgrades. By automating much of the upgrade process, we save time, reduce the risk of human error, and ensure a smoother transition to the latest version. This approach also frees up our engineering resources to focus on delivering new features and improving user experience. Maintaining backward compatibility At Rippling, ensuring backward compatibility during React Native upgrades is a critical part of our process. We aim to provide a seamless experience for our users, avoiding disruptions or issues when transitioning to the upgraded version. Here’s how we approach this: 1. Reviewing breaking changes: We meticulously analyze the React Native release notes to identify potential breaking changes. Any APIs, modules, or configurations impacted by the upgrade are flagged for review and adjustment. 2. Feature flags: We implement feature flags to isolate new features or changes. This allows us to enable or disable specific functionalities dynamically, minimizing user impact if issues arise. 3. Testing strategy: Automated testing: Comprehensive test suites ensure that existing functionalities are validated against the updated React Native version. Manual testing: Edge cases and user-specific scenarios are manually tested to catch any discrepancies not covered by automation. By prioritizing backward compatibility, we uphold our commitment to delivering a reliable and user-friendly experience while embracing the improvements offered by new React Native versions. Debugging Debugging during the upgrade process is a crucial phase that requires a meticulous and systematic approach. As you implement updates, you may encounter unexpected behaviors or errors that disrupt functionality. To efficiently address these issues, use a combination of tools that offer powerful debugging capabilities and insights into your app's performance. Debugging tools Flipper (GitHub: Flipper ): All-in-One Tool (Deprecated). Previously used for debugging at Rippling, but we have since transitioned to other tools listed below Network inspection : Proxyman (Website: Proxyman ). Used to inspect and analyze network requests and responses, ensuring the app communicates correctly with external services UI inspection : React DevTools UI Inspector (Documentation: React DevTools UI Inspector ). Helps analyze the app's UI hierarchy and components JavaScript debugging : Chrome Debugger for efficient JavaScript debugging, helping identify issues in the logic and execution flow Performance monitoring : Performance Monitor (Documentation: React Native Performance Monitor ). Used to track and address performance bottlenecks in the app Clearing caches Sometimes, issues arise from outdated cache files during the upgrade process. Clearing various caches can help resolve these problems and ensure consistency: Metro Bundler Cache : Run npx react-native start --reset-cache to reset the Metro cache. npm Cache : Use npm cache clean --force to clear the npm cache. Yarn Cache : Clear the Yarn cache by running yarn cache clean. Android Build Cache : For Android, run cd android && ./gradlew clean to clear the build cache. iOS Derived Data : Navigate to ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData and delete the contents to clear Xcode's derived data. Community resources In addition to the tools mentioned, consulting community resources such as forums and GitHub issues (e.g., React Native and Expo repositories) can provide valuable insights into common upgrade-related pitfalls. By systematically debugging and clearing caches, you can address issues more efficiently, ensuring a smoother transition to the new version of React Native and enhancing your app’s stability and performance. Testing and validation Thorough testing and validation play a critical role in ensuring the success of your React Native upgrade. A comprehensive testing strategy should include both automated and manual testing to ensure stability and a seamless user experience. Automated testing To cover all critical functionality, we utilize various tools in Rippling testing suite: Static checks : We use tools like ESLint for linting, unimported to detect unused code, TSC for type errors, and checks for cyclic dependencies to maintain code quality. Screenshot testing : We leverage react-native-owl (GitHub: react-native-owl ) for automated screenshot testing, ensuring that the UI remains consistent across updates. Unit testing : For isolated function and logic testing, Jest is our go-to framework. It helps us verify that individual components and functions are working as expected. End-to-end testing : Detox (GitHub: Detox ) is used for runtime end-to-end tests, ensuring the entire flow of the app works seamlessly in real-world scenarios. Manual testing In addition to automated testing, we perform manual testing to validate the overall user experience and identify any potential regressions that may have been missed by automation. This combination of tools and methods ensures that your app remains stable and that users enjoy a smooth, error-free experience after the upgrade. Continuous integration and deployment At Rippling, Continuous Integration (CI) and Continuous Deployment (CD) pipelines are an integral part of our overall development workflow. These pipelines automate key steps like building, testing, and deploying applications, ensuring a seamless, reliable, and efficient process for all code changes, including React Native upgrades. This approach minimizes manual intervention, reduces the risk of errors, and maintains consistent application stability and performance. We use Bitrise as our primary CI/CD platform, which allows us to: Automate builds : Every code change, including React Native version upgrades, is automatically built to ensure compatibility and identify potential issues early in the process. Run tests : Bitrise integrates with our testing framework to execute unit, integration, and end-to-end tests, ensuring that the application maintains functionality and performance post-upgrade. Streamline deployments : Upgraded builds are deployed automatically to testing environments, and eventually to production, following successful validation. By leveraging Bitrise, we maintain a consistent upgrade workflow that enhances both Rippling Mobile and Rippling Kiosk apps' stability and performance. This automation accelerates the deployment process, ensuring that users benefit from the latest features and improvements with minimal delay. Phased rollout to reduce risk of breaking changes At Rippling, we adopt a phased rollout strategy to ensure a smooth and stable transition during React Native upgrades. This dual-approach strategy minimizes risks by tailoring deployment methods based on the type of changes being introduced. For native changes , we utilize the native phased-release capabilities offered by the App Store and Google Play. These allow us to roll out updates to a percentage of users incrementally, ensuring that any issues with native components, such as updates to Android or iOS code, configuration files, or third-party libraries, can be identified and addressed early. This approach is particularly useful for updates that cannot be handled via OTA tools, such as changes to native modules or platform-specific optimizations. For JavaScript-only changes , we leverage OTA (Over-The-Air) updates using tools like Expo Updates . Previously, we relied on CodePush for OTA releases, which allowed us to gradually release changes to user subsets. With the transition to Expo Updates, we’ve gained access to a more robust feature set: Flexible rollout controls: Gradual deployments to targeted user groups help us monitor app behavior and collect feedback before broader rollouts. Enhanced rollback mechanisms: Issues can be quickly mitigated with streamlined rollback capabilities, ensuring minimal disruption for users. Improved analytics: Enhanced tracking provides detailed insights into performance and user engagement during phased rollouts. Cross-platform efficiency: Expo Updates simplifies OTA updates for both Android and iOS platforms, keeping the user experience consistent. By combining these two strategies, we ensure that Rippling Mobile and Rippling Kiosk apps maintain high performance and stability during updates. This approach enables us to balance the speed and flexibility of OTA updates with the rigor and safety of native phased releases, ensuring minimal disruption while maximizing the benefits of React Native upgrades. Monitor for issues Post-deployment monitoring is a critical step in the React Native upgrade process. Even with comprehensive testing, some issues may only surface in the production environment. At Rippling, we rely on a robust monitoring stack to proactively identify and resolve problems, ensuring a seamless user experience after each upgrade. Error monitoring with Sentry : We use Sentry to track both JavaScript and native crashes . This allows us to capture detailed error reports, including stack traces and user context, helping us quickly pinpoint and resolve issues. Sentry’s real-time alerts ensure that our team is notified immediately when a problem arises, reducing response time. Logging and performance tracking with Datadog : For deeper insights into application behavior, we leverage Datadog . It helps us track logs, monitor application performance, and identify bottlenecks or anomalies in the system. With Datadog, we gain visibility into critical metrics like API response times, memory usage, and user interactions, enabling us to maintain high performance and stability. By combining Sentry and Datadog, we create a comprehensive monitoring ecosystem that covers all aspects of our application, from JavaScript code to native modules. This proactive approach allows us to catch and address potential issues before they impact our users, ensuring a smooth post-upgrade experience for both Rippling Mobile and Rippling Kiosk apps. Update documentation After completing the upgrade, we at Rippling ensure that all internal documentation is updated to reflect the changes. This allows future developers to easily understand the rationale behind the upgrade, as well as any new features or modifications. Keeping the documentation thorough and up-to-date is key to maintaining project continuity and facilitating a smoother transition for anyone working on the codebase in the future. Conclusion Upgrading your React Native application may seem daunting, but with the right approach, it can be a seamless process that unlocks significant benefits. At Rippling, we've honed our strategy to ensure smooth transitions while minimizing disruptions. Here’s a recap of key takeaways: Adopt a gradual approach: Break the upgrade into smaller, manageable steps to reduce risks and improve stability. Scope effectively: Clearly identify necessary changes and prioritize them to focus on what's most impactful. Leverage automation: Use tools like Bitrise and Expo Updates to streamline upgrade, testing, and deployment processes. Maintain backward compatibility: Safeguard existing functionality to ensure a seamless experience for all users. Prioritize testing and validation: Implement robust testing strategies, including automated and manual testing, to identify issues early. Utilize CI/CD pipelines: Integrate upgrades into your CI/CD processes for efficient testing and reliable deployment. By adopting these practices, you can not only minimize the challenges associated with upgrading but also maximize the value of new features, security patches, and performance enhancements that each new React Native version brings. Upgrading isn’t just a maintenance task—it’s a critical step toward keeping your application future-proof and delivering the best possible experience to your users. We're hiring engineers! title: Local Legends: Animal Crackers, Where Customers Become Family
summary: Watch Local Legends: Animal Crackers Where Customers Become Family and explore more insights from Brixmor on retail, redevelopment, and community. Check out the latest from our blog.
body_text: Community-driven retail builds lasting loyalty When small businesses create meaningful connections with their customers, they do more than sell products. They become part of the community. Animal Crackers in Plano, Texas is a clear example of how a locally owned retailer can grow into a destination that keeps generations coming back. For more than 30 years, Animal Crackers has built a loyal following by delivering a warm and personal shopping experience. Customers are not just shoppers. They are treated like family. From knowing customer preferences and sizes to going above and beyond with thoughtful service, the team has created a place where people feel recognized, valued, and excited to return. Located in an open-air retail center, the store benefits from strong visibility, steady foot traffic, and a walkable environment that encourages discovery. Combined with a bright and playful atmosphere, a curated mix of products, and a beloved shop dog, Animal Crackers offers more than retail. It creates a memorable local experience. This is what happens when the right tenant meets the right retail environment. In this video, you will see: • How personalized service builds multi-generational customer loyalty • Why community first retailers drive repeat visits and strong engagement • The role of open-air retail centers in increasing foot traffic and discovery • How local ownership creates deeper customer relationships • Why experiential shopping encourages customers to keep coming back Why it matters: Community rooted businesses like Animal Crackers do more than operate in a center. They elevate it. Their ability to create connection, loyalty, and consistent traffic strengthens overall performance and supports long term value for the entire retail environment.

title: TWO Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
body_text: TWO Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results July 28, 2026 4:15pm EDT Download as PDF Related Documents NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- TWO (Two Harbors Investment Corp., NYSE: TWO), an MSR-focused real estate investment trust (REIT), today announced its financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Quarterly Summary Continued to advance toward closing of merger with CrossCountry Mortgage, LLC (CCM). Pursuant to the definitive merger agreement, as amended, CCM will acquire all of the outstanding shares of TWO common stock for $12.00 per share. Holders of TWO’s Series A, Series B and Series C Preferred Stock will have their shares redeemed following the closing of the transaction at $25.00 per share, plus any accumulated and unpaid dividends, in accordance with the terms of the preferred stock. On July 2, 2026, TWO common stockholders approved the merger; the transaction is expected to close on August 3, 2026, subject to the satisfaction of certain remaining closing conditions. On July 23, 2026, declared a “stub period” dividend of $0.12196 per share of common stock for the third quarter of 2026, subject to the consummation of the merger. Reported book value of $10.68 per common share, and declared a second quarter common stock dividend of $0.34 per share, representing a 4.3% quarterly economic return on book value.(1) Generated comprehensive income of $47.9 million, or $0.45 per weighted average basic common share. Added $186.5 million in unpaid principal balance (UPB) of MSR through flow-sale acquisitions and recapture. As of June 30, 2026, MSR portfolio had a weighted average gross coupon rate of 3.54% and a 60+ day delinquency rate of 0.79%, and had experienced a 3-month CPR of 6.3%. Funded $84.0 million UPB in loans and brokered an additional $48.8 million UPB in second lien loans. ____________________ (1) Economic return on book value is defined as the increase (decrease) in common book value from the beginning to the end of the given period, plus dividends declared to common stockholders in the period, divided by common book value as of the beginning of the period. title: AI in finance operating layer beneath the demo: data, controls, workflow, risk, trust and decisions
body_text: Everyone has seen the AI demo. A prompt goes in. A polished answer appears. A dashboard lights up. A process that normally takes hours seems to collapse into seconds. The demo matters because it makes the possibility visible. But for financial-services leaders, possibility is no longer the hard part. The hard part begins on Monday morning, when the system has to work inside real processes, real controls and real customer expectations. That is where the next advantage in AI will be won—not on the presentation screen, but in the operating layer underneath it. The demo is the surface. The operating model is the product. A financial institution does not create value because a model can generate an impressive response. Value appears when the model can work with the right data, enter the right workflow, respect the right controls and help the business make a better decision. That distinction is easy to miss. A demo is designed to show what AI can do under clean conditions. An operating system has to survive incomplete records, exceptions, approval limits, legacy infrastructure, regulatory scrutiny and customers whose lives do not fit neatly into a test case. The question is therefore not, “Can the model do this?” It is, “Can our institution make this useful, safe and repeatable?” Six layers determine whether AI becomes useful 1. Data quality. AI cannot repair an operating model built on inaccessible, inconsistent or poorly governed information. Institutions need clear sources of truth, reliable document intake and permissioned access before the model can act with confidence. 2. Workflow. An answer is not an outcome. The system needs a defined path from detection or recommendation to the next approved action. Who receives the case? What can happen automatically? Where must a person intervene? What closes the loop? 3. Controls. Financial services runs on authority, not just intelligence. Every useful AI workflow needs boundaries: identity checks, role-based access, approval thresholds, audit trails and clear limits on what the system may change. 4. Risk. A model can be accurate on average and still fail badly in the cases that matter most. Teams need to understand error costs, escalation rules, bias, fraud exposure and what happens when confidence is low. 5. Customer trust. Faster is not automatically better. A claims decision, payment exception or support response must still be understandable, contestable and fair. Customers should know when a person is available and should not have to restart their story at every handoff. 6. Decisions. The final test is whether AI improves a business decision. Did the claim move with better context? Was fraud identified earlier? Did reconciliation release trapped cash? Did support resolve the request instead of producing another explanation? Where the real value is beginning to show up The strongest AI use cases in finance are often less visible than the chatbot on the homepage. They sit inside the work: Claims: extracting information from documents, detecting missing evidence, prioritising cases and helping authorised teams make faster, better-supported decisions. Fraud and risk: finding patterns across transactions or claims, surfacing anomalies earlier and giving investigators a clearer starting point. Reconciliation: matching records, identifying exceptions and routing the unresolved items that quietly trap cash and time. Customer operations: moving from generic answers to verified retrieval, approved actions and context-rich human escalation. Underwriting and decision support: bringing more relevant information into the decision while keeping judgement, governance and accountability visible. None of these outcomes comes from a model alone. Each one depends on the surrounding operating layer. The Monday-morning test for any AI initiative Before approving the next pilot, financial-services teams should ask seven practical questions: 1. Which specific decision or workflow are we improving? 2. What data will the system use, and who is authorised to access it? 3. What can the AI recommend, and what can it actually do? 4. Where are the mandatory human checkpoints? 5. How will errors, exceptions and customer disputes be handled? 6. What evidence will show that the workflow is creating value? 7. Who owns the result after the pilot ends? If those questions are unanswered, the project is still a demo, even if the interface looks finished. AI advantage is an organisational capability The institutions that pull ahead will not necessarily be the ones with the most models. They will be the ones that learn how to turn models into governed operating capability. That requires cross-functional work. Strategy can identify where advantage may exist. Operations understands the process and its exceptions. Technology connects the system. Risk and compliance define the boundaries. Product translates capability into an experience. Commercial and finance test whether the value is real. When these teams work in sequence, AI gets trapped in pilots and handoffs. When they work together, the organisation can decide faster what to scale, what to redesign and what not to automate. Why AI Compass is built around the layer beneath the demo AI Compass Lagos brings financial-services operators, builders and decision-makers into one room to compare what is real across insurance, banking, payments, fintech and embedded finance. The conversation is not another broad debate about whether AI matters. It is about what survives production: the data, controls, workflows, risk decisions and customer expectations that determine whether AI creates operating advantage. On 13 August 2026 at Radisson Blu Anchorage in Lagos, teams will examine where AI is already changing financial services, where the gaps remain and what is worth building next. If your team is moving from AI possibility to operating advantage, register for AI Compass Lagos . Bring the strategist, the operator, the builder and the person responsible for trust when the system goes live. The takeaway Everyone has seen the AI demo. The next advantage will belong to the institutions that can make AI work after the room empties. The model is only one part of the system. Data quality, workflow, controls, risk, customer trust and decision discipline are what turn intelligence into value. The real question is no longer whether AI can impress us. It is whether we can build the operating conditions that let it earn trust and deliver results.

body_text: Winnipeg, Manitoba–(Newsfile Corp. – July 7, 2026) – Frontier Nuclear and Minerals Inc. (NASDAQ: FNUC) (“Frontier”) , a nuclear fuel cycle company, announces that it has signed an agreement with DISA Technologies Inc. (“ DISA “) to characterize and remediate legacy uranium mine waste dumps and to recover saleable uranium at Frontier’s 100% owned Maybell uranium project (the “ Maybell Project “) in Colorado. Environmental remediation and uranium recovery will occur simultaneously at the former Maybell uranium mine Highlights: DISA will deploy its patented High-Pressure Slurry Ablation (“ HPSA™ “) system in modular mobile plants to recover saleable uranium and other critical mineral concentrates from waste dumps at the Maybell Project Frontier Nuclear will be paid a net revenue royalty based on a sliding scale royalty rate of between 2.5% to 4% based on uranium price and derived from the sale of uranium and other critical minerals extracted from the waste dumps at the Maybell Project DISA will operate the waste remediation program at the Maybell Project and pay all associated costs No capital or operating costs will be payable by Frontier A total of 17 separate prospective waste dumps have been identified through ground surveys at the Maybell Project to date, and others may be added over time HPSA™ is a patented, chemical-free, modular process that selectively separates uranium and other target minerals from waste material using high-velocity slurry collisions.1 CEO Remarks “We are pleased to have partnered with DISA to apply its breakthrough process to remediate abandoned uranium mine waste at our Maybell Project, and to recover valuable uranium and critical minerals, while addressing the environmental impacts of historical uranium mining,” said Frank Wheatley, CEO of Frontier. “With uranium demand at multi-decade highs and the U.S. Government actively prioritizing domestic critical mineral recovery, the timing could not be better to unlock the value contained in our Maybell Project’s legacy waste dumps.” Next Steps: DISA will: Launch a characterisation programme with a combination of assay and gamma probe to determine likely quantities of uranium and other recoverable minerals present in the waste dumps, expected to take approximately six months Apply for all requisite permits necessary to commence treatment of waste and recovery of payable concentrates using HPSA™ technology Pay Frontier a net revenue royalty on future sales of metals concentrates Advantages of HPSA ™ : The HPSA™ process treats surface dumps of previously partially mined and aggregated material, and has been independently validated through a U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (“ EPA “) treatability study (“ EPA Study “) conducted at three Navajo abandoned uranium mine sites in 2022 and published in December 2023 In September 2025, DISA became the first company to receive a Service Providers License from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, providing a regulatory license for DISA to remediate legacy uranium mine waste. DISA can now recover valuable uranium and critical minerals, and more importantly, leave the environment significantly improved There is strong US Government support for domestic recovery of uranium and critical minerals from legacy mine waste. This activity is directly in line with the recent Secretarial Order No. 3436, which directs federal agencies to prioritize domestic recovery of critical and strategic minerals from mine waste U.S. EPA Study The EPA Study, carried out by Tetra Tech Inc. under EPA contract, found that the HPSA™ process reduced uranium concentrations in treated material by between 61% and 94% depending on waste characteristics, with comparable reductions in radium-226. A particularly significant finding: the process concentrates more than 90% of the uranium content into a fines fraction that represents just 17% of total processed mass — leaving the bulk of the treated material clean enough to remain on site and dramatically reducing the volume of material requiring regulated disposal. The EPA confirmed the HPSA™ process as a viable treatment technology for abandoned uranium mine waste on Navajo Nation lands and on other state and federal lands, a conclusion directly applicable to legacy mine waste sites such as the Maybell Project. The full study is publicly available on the EPA website.2 Maybell Uranium Project The Maybell Project, 100% owned by Frontier, is located at the southern end of the Sand Wash Basin between the towns of Maybell and Lay in Moffat County, Colorado. It covers an area of approximately 9,497 acres and is comprised of 480 Federal mining claims (8,857 acres) and one State Exploration Lease (640 acres). The Maybell Project has witnessed historical production of approximately 5.3Mlbs U3O8 over two discrete historical mining periods. The location of the waste dumps on the Maybell Project are set out in Figure 1, attached as Schedule A. About DISA Technologies Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Casper, Wyoming, DISA Technologies focuses on upgrading critical minerals from mined ore and legacy waste, serving both mining and remediation sectors. DISA’s technology isolates targeted minerals from ores and legacy waste, including precious and industrial metals, hydrocarbons, and uranium, aiming to reduce costs and environmental impact while enhancing mineral processing and environmental remediation.3 About Frontier Nuclear and Minerals Inc. Frontier Nuclear and Minerals Inc. is focused on building a U.S.-based nuclear fuel cycle platform through uranium exploration and development assets, together with targeted investments in Ubaryon Pty. Ltd., a private Australian company developing next generation enrichment technology, and Kadmos Energy Services LLC, a private U.S. company developing small modular light water reactors. Frontier continues to evaluate opportunities in the nuclear fuel cycle that align with its long-term strategic objectives. title: 3 success factors for moving payments to the public cloud
summary: This CGI blog post discusses three success factors for moving payments to the public cloud.
body_text: By Karen Brown The concept of security intertwines with the banking industry at its very core. After all, what is a bank if not a place that promises to keep its customers’ money and information safe? So, maybe it is only natural that some decision-makers in the banking industry are reticent to consider moving payments to the public cloud. While many bank executives are confident the private cloud is secure, they continue to balk at moving their core systems—or “crown jewels” as one of our clients calls them—to the public cloud. However, banks that fail to consider moving their data centers to the public cloud are missing out. First, they could end up left behind by their competition. Of the 264 banking executives we interviewed face-to-face as part of our 2021 CGI Voice of Our Clients program, 60% said they are planning to migrate at least 21% of their applications to the cloud over the next 2 years. The promise of the cloud for banks includes a long list of advantages, including: Sustainability Resource elasticity Reduced capacity planning Improved resiliency Increased efficiency Lower costs Now is actually a great time for forward-looking banks to consider the public cloud as a way to become even more agile and sustainable while lowering costs. The adoption of real-time, 24/7 payments already is a reality for many banks, and this trend continues to advance globally. Moving payments to the public cloud securely and seamlessly is not only feasible but transformative, if done the right way. Here are three factors to consider before moving payments to the public cloud. Select a multi-cloud-native and cloud-agnostic payments platform Selecting the platform is the first step. Moving your core payments infrastructure to the public cloud requires a fit-for-purpose, multi-cloud-native, cloud-independent solution that is ready to make the most of the cloud’s benefits. Look for a payments platform that provides interoperability to avoid tying your organization down to a specific cloud platform—a mistake that virtually guarantees technical debt down the road. In addition, make sure the platform is engineered to deliver the orchestration and real-time, 24-hour processing required for success. Find a partner with extensive cloud infrastructure and deployment experience As good as your payments platform may be, it will fall short without the right experience for deploying it. Team up with a partner that has proven cloud infrastructure expertise along with experience in implementing related cloud processes. In addition, choose a partner with knowledge about minimizing risks, costs and business disruption during deployment. It’s also important to find a partner with professionals who are trained and certified in process implementation specifically for banking institutions, and those who are experienced in monitoring and troubleshooting the platform once it is deployed. These services should be thoroughly documented and auditable for when banking regulators come calling. Implement advanced security controls with a strong risk management approach Success factor number three brings us back to where we started. Banking payments can happen securely in the public cloud—but the right kind of security is critical. Leaders in the public cloud space already have substantial cybersecurity features built into their platforms. However, the job of further hardening a specific environment, like one where financial transactions take place, falls to your organization and the team managing your public cloud deployment. Cloud security controls, like NIST 800 and regulatory customer security controls, are critical for making payments secure and require set up by someone who knows how to apply them with maximum efficiency. Ultimately, we recommend investment in a set of security tools that balances the goals of limiting risk, avoiding disruption and minimizing cost. Anything with the word “public” in it is going to get a good, long (and, sometimes, skeptical) look from security-minded banking leaders. However, the number of banks that have made the leap successfully is growing, and I predict that—within a year or so—public cloud deployment of payments infrastructure will be the norm. As a result, digital leaders in the banking space who are in front of that trend will be the first to enjoy its advantages. At CGI, we reimagined and reengineered our payments platform, CGI All Payments, to support both public and private cloud deployments. To learn more about it, read our paper on moving payments to the public cloud or visit our CGI All Payments page on cgi.com. In addition, feel free to reach out to me for further discussion.
